subjects.displayTitle: Happiness: gratitude, inward freedom, and the joy we give
subjects.introduction: An old man wrapped his samovar in a saddlebag each afternoon, carried it to a meadow, and marvelled at the colour of his tea. People said kings were not so happy. His gladness owed nothing to possessions, and that is where ‘Abdu’l-Bahá begins: happiness is a star in every heart, hidden only by clouds, and a candle lit in the heart drives out the gloom of evil suggestions. He called his own forty years of imprisonment years of supreme joy, and likened the heart to an ocean, storm-tossed on the surface, calm in its depths. Yet this inward freedom turns outward at once, into the command to bring joy to hearts, to console the sad, to keep a cheerful face for the sake of the glad tidings within. Sorrow is given its place, and joy promised after it. The Dhammapada’s picture of living happily and without hostility among the hostile offers a companion from another tradition [1]. From here the journey leads to serenity, to humour within a balanced life, to the radiant countenance that lightens other people, and to the virtuous life in which joy finally rests.
subjects.arc: Begin with everyday gratitude and bringing joy to others, explore the sources and meanings of spiritual happiness, listen to accounts of joy amid trials, then return to fellowship, character, and generous action.

order.why: Turn immediately toward comforting and assisting others.
shortened: Turn all your thoughts toward bringing joy to hearts. Beware! Beware! lest ye offend any heart. Assist the world of humanity as much as possible. Be the source of consolation to every sad one, assist every weak one, be helpful to every indigent one, care for every sick one, be the cause of glorification to every lowly one, and shelter those who are overshadowed by fear.

order.why: Open with delight in tea, a meadow, and ordinary blessings.
Connect happiness with character and the well-being of every person.
shortened: The purpose of the foregoing statements is to demonstrate at least this, that the happiness and greatness, the rank and station, the pleasure and peace, of an individual have never consisted in his personal wealth, but rather in his excellent character, his high resolve, the breadth of his learning, and his ability to solve difficult problems.

The primary purpose, the basic objective, in laying down powerful laws and setting up great principles and institutions dealing with every aspect of civilization, is human happiness; and human happiness consists only in drawing closer to the Threshold of Almighty God, and in securing the peace and well-being of every individual member, high and low alike, of the human race; and the supreme agencies for accomplishing these two objectives are the excellent qualities with which humanity has been endowed.

order.why: Allow spiritual and physical happiness to enrich one another.
Make room for sorrow within the promise of joy to follow.
shortened: God willing, may you be joyous at all times, and should any sorrow touch you, know with certainty that after it joy is ordained. Indeed, divine bounty towards thee is beyond reckoning.

order.why: Read the image of a home that sends people away with glad hearts.
shortened: If the candle of happiness is ignited in the chamber of the heart all the foreboding gloom of evil suggestions will be dispelled.

My home is the home of happiness. My home is the home of Unity. My home is the home of Peace. My home is the home of joy and delight. My home is the home of laughter and exultation. Whosoever enters through the portals of this home must go out with a gladsome heart. This is the home of Light, whosoever enters therein must become illumined.

order.why: Consider the ocean’s calm depths beneath its changing surface.
shortened: This is what causes joy in the human heart - to be accepted at the threshold of the Divine Unity. Then one's heart is always in the utmost gladness, and even if trials and tribulations assail from all sides, the heart remains joyful. It is like an ocean - waves and storms may be seen on its surface, but its depths remain calm and tranquil.

order.why: Read the reported exchange asking where happiness comes from.
shortened: A man asked another: "In what station are you?" He answered: "In the utmost happiness." "Where does this happiness come from?"

order.why: Read the inward star and the clouds that obscure it.
Hear the invitation to rejoice and reflect beauty.
Join joy with trust and contentment.
shortened: Live in the world with joy and delight, then build thy affairs upon trust in God and contentment.

order.why: Follow knowledge and devotion into fairness, forbearance, and generosity.
shortened: Happiness lies in knowledge, and knowledge in the fear of God, and the fear of God in detachment and aversion from worldly ornaments. And detachment brings divine love, and love seeks the recitation of verses and communes with God, and the attraction of verses refines character - that is, truthfulness in the path of God and fairness with people and mastery over self and association with the righteous and avoidance of the ignorant and respect for the great ones and kindness to the lesser ones and giving counsel to friends and forbearance with enemies and generosity to the poor and love for all people and guidance of those who have gone astray.
This is the most great happiness and the supreme gift and the imperishable bounty.

order.why: Introduce the distinction between physical and spiritual happiness.
shortened: O maidservant of God! Happiness is of two kinds: one is physical, the other spiritual. The former is finite: it lasteth a day, a month, perhaps a year, and ultimately yieldeth nothing. But the latter is endless and eternal; it revealeth itself through the love of God, and is attained through virtues and perfections in the world of humanity.

order.why: Distinguishes passing natural enjoyment from enduring spiritual happiness.
Read the reported companion distinction in its own terms.
shortened: Happiness is of two kinds : physical, possessed by animals and men, and spiritual, which is known only by those men who have attained to holiness. Physical pleasure is something casual and temporary only-is due to an adventitious and transient condition of the nerves. But spiritual joy is of God and is unending.

order.why: Explore the extended account of spiritual happiness as love and life.
shortened: As to spiritual happiness, this is the true basis of the life of man because life is created for happiness, not for sorrow; for pleasure, not for grief. Happiness is life; sorrow is death. Spiritual happiness is eternal. This is a light which is not followed by darkness. This is an honor which is not followed by shame. This is a life that is not followed by death. This is an existence that is not followed by annihilation. This great blessing and precious gift is obtained by man only through the guidance of God.
This happiness is but the love of God.

order.why: Consider the reported relation between spiritual life and happiness.
shortened: As for the spiritual perfections they are man's birthright and belong to him alone of all creation. Man is, in reality, a spiritual being, and only when he lives in the spirit is he truly happy.

order.why: Read the distinction between lasting and fleeting enjoyment.
shortened: The purport is that the heart of man receives happiness through the fragrances of the paradise of Abha and the breaths of the Holy Spirit. Mundane things do not bring any lasting happiness. Earthly happiness endures but for an hour or two.

order.why: Consider the report’s image of material happiness as an unstable structure.
shortened: Do not believe for one moment that it is possible for man to obtain happiness, joy, serenity and confidence save through God. If his heart is not attached to God no matter how seemingly permanent is the structure of his material happiness it will totter down.

order.why: Read the vulnerability of happiness tied to possessions and circumstances.
shortened: Therefore we must be happy.

Happiness must be in GOD. When people are happy in wealth, wealth may disappear. When they are happy in children, the children may die. If it is in luxury, it may be taken away. Therefore, eternal happiness is impossible for man except in GOD.

order.why: Consider hopes, desires, and the source of spiritual joy.
shortened: When you look at reality, there is no one without desire, and no desire is free from trouble and weariness.

Therefore every kind of hope becomes the cause of difficulty and burden, and prevents joy and happiness - except the hopes of souls who bind themselves to the divine world. They attain spiritual joy and achieve conscious happiness.

order.why: Read the reported orientation toward the Kingdom.
shortened: Therefore, man thinks his happiness is from this world and what it contains, while God has created him in such manner that his happiness must come from the Kingdom; that is, he must find joy from the spiritual world.

order.why: Keep the report’s categorical claim about happiness and God attributed to its source.
Consider outward luxury beside inward restlessness.
shortened: Then the comfort of this world also will be thine. All these men thou art beholding are not enjoying happiness, and are heavily laden with misery of some kind or another. If they sleep on couches of velvet and silk, yet they are sad and restless:
But when the believers of God free themselves from these entangling ties and become spiritual, sanctified and purified, they receive the real joy of this life and their hearts are at ease.

order.why: Read the critique of limited conceptions of enjoyment as the source’s challenge.
shortened: How negligent people are! What insignificant things they consider necessary for their happiness! How negligent they are! Like unto animals, they eat, they sleep, they walk, they sing, they dance, and after the manner of their kind think they are having a good time. But in truth the animals are better off, for without toil or trouble they enjoy all the material blessings necessary for their existence.

order.why: Join knowledge of God with humanitarian deeds.
shortened: This happiness is age-abiding!

If a person is thirsty for the water of the Knowledge of God, his happiness is unfailing. If a soul is interested in humanitarian deeds, his joy is perennial. Therefore. The happiness that comes through God is a light that is not followed by any darkness; a healing which is not ended by any disease; a glory which is not consummated by any shame.

order.why: Explore the many images of happiness, including goodwill and forgiveness.
shortened: Happiness is the cherubim of the Almighty which inspires mankind to perform feats of self-sacrifice and deeds of disinterested philanthropy. Happiness is the melodious-singing nightingale which transforms the darkened world of sorrow into the beaming-realm of celestial beatitude. Happiness is the waving ocean in the depth of which the diver finds the pearls of resignation and the corals of renunciation. Happiness is the elysium wherein grows the asphodels of good-will and the amaranths of forgiveness.

order.why: Consider how inward joy changes the experience of outward surroundings.
Read hope and light in the account of faith.
shortened: But when the light of faith shines forth in the realm of the heart, eternal joy appears and the darkness of sorrow and gloom vanishes away. The despairing one becomes filled with hope, and the sorrowful one is immersed in the sea of gladness. This is an eternal joy that is followed by no sorrow.

order.why: Keep the chalice and star as images of enduring gladness.
shortened: Be thou stirred with the Divine Glad tidings so that thou mayst hold in thy grasp the Chalice of imperishable Happiness and discover the brilliant star of age-abiding felicity and rest!

order.why: Read the garden, water, dream, and breeze imagery.
Consider connection with another realm in the invitation to joy.
shortened: Therefore, turn your attention entirely to another world and establish your connection to another realm, so that all your days may pass in joy upon joy, and all your times may bring forth eternal gladness.

order.why: Read praise, remembrance, and love together.
Hear the reported account of love changing despondency.
shortened: The love of Baha'u'llah is the essence of happiness, Any heart which will become the depository of this love is always happy. There have been many people sad and despondent but as soon as the sun of the love of Baha'u'llah shone in their hearts they became happy.

order.why: Keep the concise reported statement about love with its source omission.
shortened: Nothing makes a man so happy as love...

order.why: Read the response to visitors distressed about their own faults.
shortened: One day at luncheon Abdu'l-Baha asked us if we were glad to be at Akka and if we were happy. We answered that we were very happy to be there with Him but that when we thought of our faults we were unhappy. He replied emphatically, "Think not of yourselves, but think of the Bounty of God. This will always make you happy."

order.why: Consider detachment as freedom and lightness.
shortened: To be detached is to be free, is to be flying in a new ether, is to be light, is to be joyous - and a Bahai should be joyous. He should attain to such a station of joy that the world will enquire as to his secret.

order.why: Read the aspiration to inward peace amid changing circumstances.
Keep the report’s account of joy beyond the fulfillment of personal hopes.
shortened: This happiness is eternal and the cause of expansion of heart and soul in all divine worlds. When one's happiness is from divine bounties, they will not become sad or sorrowful in any condition, even if worldly events are not according to their desires and the turning of fortune does not promote their hopes and thoughts.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast between little food and real affluence.
shortened: But those who have faith in God act according to the divine teachings; even though they need a little food to survive, they will pass their lives in the utmost happiness and joy. This is one of the bounties of religion; this is eternal happiness, life everlasting and real affluence.

order.why: Read the recollection of joy during imprisonment as a personal testimony.
shortened: I myself was in prison forty years -- one year alone would have been impossible to bear -- nobody survived that imprisonment more than a year! But, thank God, during all those forty years I was supremely happy! Every day, on waking, it was like hearing good tidings, and every night infinite joy was mine. Spirituality was my comfort, and turning to God was my greatest joy. If this had not been so, do you think it possible that I could have lived through those forty years in prison?

order.why: Hear the distinction between bodily suffering and spiritual gladness.
Consider the remembered joy of exile despite material deprivation.
Read shared thin soup as a concrete scene of happiness.
Keep the reported scene of thirteen people sharing one room.
shortened: At one time in Acca, thirteen Bahais lived in one room, but they radiated peace, joy and love.

order.why: Read the account of joy amid restrictions and confinement.
shortened: Notwithstanding these restrictions and this confinement we were in the utmost joy; our breasts were dilated with the happiness of the Kingdom, our trust was in the Mercy of the Lord, our hearts were attracted with the Fragrances of God and our souls rejoiced by the Glad-tidings of Truth.

order.why: Keep the brief reported recollection of imprisonment in its own form.
Read the rose and nightingale imagery under tests and persecution.
shortened: During the time of Peace, security, Comfort and the lack of sorrow, even the monkey will be the most jovial fellow. He will be happy, joyful, grateful, patient and overflowing with gladsomeness. But the sincere servant of Baha'u'llah, who is firm in the Covenant and steadfast in the Testament, while surrounded by the most great sea of tests; threatened by the surging, rocking waves of persecution and encircled by the whirlwinds of calumnies and backbiting - will blossom like unto a rose and breaks into joyous songs and sweet melodies like unto the nightingale.

order.why: Consider the source’s praise of contentment in hardship.
shortened: The necessity and the particularity of the assured and believing ones is to be firm in the Cause of God and withstand the hidden and evident tests. Thanks be to God that you are distinguished and made eminent by this blessing. Anybody can be happy in the state of comfort, ease, health, success, pleasure and joy; but if one will be happy and contented in the time of trouble, hardship and prevailing disease, it is the proof of nobility.

order.why: Read service and love in the image of the bitter cup.
shortened: However, it behooveth thee to serve the Threshold of the All-Merciful with the utmost assurance, steadfastness and certitude, for these trials and tribulations are in the path of the All-Glorious, and this bitter cup must be drunk with the utmost joy and gladness out of love for the Abha Beauty.

order.why: Consider solidarity with the trials of loved ones, retaining the source omission.
shortened: Yet from another perspective, consider that the loved ones of God are intoxicated from the overflowing cup of trials, and their joy and gladness lie in bearing afflictions and tribulations in the path of God.
Rather, we must find joy and gladness that, to the extent of our capacity and ability, we share in the trials of God's loved ones.

order.why: Read the counsel concerning joy amid harm in its devotional setting.
Hear the invitation to remain radiant in the meadow of trials.
shortened: Therefore, do not be tested by trials and tribulations, and like a flower be radiant in this meadow so that you may find spiritual joy and seek conscious delight.

order.why: Keep the account of believers approaching martyrdom in its historical and devotional terms.
shortened: Those who had eyes to see rejoiced at the glad tidings and cried out: 'O blessed, blessed are we!', and they witnessed the inner reality of all things, and uncovered the mysteries of the Kingdom. Delivered then from their fancies and their doubts, they beheld the light of truth, and so exhilarated did they become from draining the chalice of God's love, that they utterly forgot the world and their own selves. Dancing for joy they hastened to the place of their own martyrdom and there, where men die for love, they flung away their heads and hearts.

order.why: Read the reported metaphor of sorrow as fruitful furrows.
Keep the report’s severe comparison of life and death in its own wording; do not turn it into counsel to a distressed reader.
Read the aging emperor story and health assertions as features of the report.
Keep the reported language of joy as a cure attributed to its source.
Read the companion statement about joy and illness in its source setting.
Consider the image of happiness as food.
Read the encouragement concerning health, livelihood, and vocation.
shortened: You must live in the utmost happiness. If any trouble or vicissitude comes into your lives, if your heart is depressed on account of health, livelihood or vocation, let not these things affect you. They should not cause unhappiness, for Baha'u'llah has brought you divine happiness. He has prepared heavenly food for you; He has destined eternal bounty for you; He has bestowed everlasting glory upon you. Therefore, these glad tidings should cause you to soar in the atmosphere of joy forever and ever.

order.why: Hear the invitation to fresh spirit and renewed joy.
Consider confidence and gratitude within the sheltering-shade image.
Read the aspiration to an expanded heart.
shortened: Be joyful within yourself and grieve not over anything, and maintain such an expanded heart that it shall never be contracted.

order.why: Hear the encouragement addressed to one person’s love and knowledge.
shortened: Beware, beware lest you grieve over anything, for grief extinguishes the warmth of your love. Rather, be joyful in what God has given you of His love and knowledge, and soon the door of blessings will open to you from all directions.

order.why: Join gladness with reminding others of revealed words.
Keep the concise call to join the joyous.
Read consolation through remembrance of divine favors.
shortened: In any case, forget sorrows and complaints, and hearken to the melody of the Abha Kingdom. Be joyous and delighted, show forth eagerness and ardor, for praise be to God, thou art established beneath the favors of the Most Glorious Beauty, art immortalized in the paradise of the good-pleasure of the Servant of Baha, art regarded by the glance of the Lord of Oneness, and art known and described in the Supreme Concourse as the herald of the Covenant.

order.why: Consider the devotional invitation to move beyond preoccupation with self.
shortened: Let us put aside all thoughts of self; let us close our eyes to all on earth, let us neither make known our sufferings nor complain of our wrongs. Rather let us become oblivious of our own selves, and drinking down the wine of heavenly grace, let us cry out our joy, and lose ourselves in the beauty of the All-Glorious.

order.why: Read joy and sorrow together as oriented toward God.
shortened: O Faraj! Let thy joy and gladness and sorrow be for God alone. Be happy in truth and confident in truth, and be sorrowful only for His sake.

The radiant effulgence of the Sun of Joy hath taken hold of thee and the Tongue of Eternity speaketh with thee. I swear by the sweetness of the utterance of the All-Merciful that oceans of joy are concealed in this mention.

order.why: Keep the counsel to focus on God amid differences.
shortened: Be in the utmost joy and delight and fix your gaze on naught but God, for the winds of differences are blowing from all directions.

order.why: Read the wine imagery in the promise of joy.
shortened: If thou shouldst drink of this wine, such joy shall possess thee that the troubles and sorrows of the world will never seize thee.

order.why: Hear glad tidings sent from prison to communities facing calamities.
shortened: O friends! Gather together with joy and fragrance, and with perfect wisdom and utterance, and drink of the most pure and luminous wine in the name of the Lord of Power. Verily it is My wondrous love, My cherished word, and My holy, transcendent, sublime remembrance. Be not saddened by the calamities of the world. By God! The ocean of joy yearns for your presence, for every good thing hath been created for you and will appear according to the requirements of time. Thus doth My Most Exalted Pen give you glad tidings from this Most Great Prison as a bounty from Him, and He is the All-Bountiful, the Most Generous."

order.why: Consider the celebration of the days of God.
Read the rising Sun of Joy as a question addressed to the heart.
Consider rejoicing extending through creation and scripture.
shortened: Today all things, the Concourse on High, the divine Books and holy Scriptures, some in the innermost mystery and others openly and manifestly, are engaged in joy and delight, for this is the Most Great Day of rejoicing.

order.why: Keep the account of the day’s joy and divine coming.
Read hearing and sight as ways of perceiving joy in all things.
Consider opened gates and the imagery of resurrection.
Hear the proclamation of a season of rejoicing.
shortened: This is the day of rejoicing and the hour of ecstasy! This is the season of the dead arising from the graves and gathering together! And this is the promised time for the attainment of plenteous grace.

order.why: Read the assurance of an extraordinary station.
Consider the particular community’s season of gladness.
shortened: O beloved friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Spend day and night in joy, gladness, delight and success, for the Blessed Beauty is pleased with you and this afflicted servant is grateful. It is a time of joy, a season of delight, days of gladness and a period of success.

order.why: Read the invitation to live as in celebration of Naw Ruz.
Join gratitude with creating joy and promoting the Faith.
shortened: Therefore, O friends, show gratitude for this manifest bounty and with soul and consciousness create joy and delight. Take up an overflowing cup, raise a resurrection, be happy and successful, and promote the Faith of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison with earlier dispensations in its source terms.
Read the questions about joy beside the imagery of fruitful trees.
shortened: You have turned to the kingdom of Baha'u'llah and are manifesting the favors of Baha'u'llah. Verily the light of the Most Great Guidance has become iridescent in your hearts, and in the wilderness of the world you are proving to be fruitful trees. What reward is greater than this? This is a great bounty, a great bestowal. If you be not happy, who could be happy? If you be not attracted, who could be attracted? If you be not radiant, who could be radiant? If you fly not away with joy, who could fly away?

order.why: Hear the reported call to live and rejoice.
Keep the repeated encouragement to confidence and hope.
Read the encouragement offered to departing Seattle believers.
Consider reassurance of companionship during a journey.
shortened: You will be very happy, for I will be with you all the way. You must go with the utmost happiness and cheerfulness.

order.why: Hear the stated wish for the Portland believers’ happiness.
Read the wish for security and joy addressed to a friend.
shortened: O thou kind friend! Through the bounties of the Blessed Beauty, my wish for thee is that thou mayest ever remain secure, protected and joyful.

order.why: Consider the reported desire to provide comfort and prosperity.
Hear the prayer for hearts and souls to be gladdened, with its omission retained.
shortened: At all times do I speak of you and call you to mind. I pray unto the Lord, and with tears I implore Him to rain down all these blessings upon you, and gladden your hearts, and make blissful your souls, and grant you exceeding joy and heavenly delights...

order.why: Read the prayer for opened doors, even roads, and spiritual joy.
Keep the concise hope for gladness to appear.
Consider drinking from the ocean of joy.
shortened: God willing, may you ever drink from the ocean of joy and remain fixed in contemplation of the Most Glorious Horizon.

order.why: Join the Kawthar of joy with morning and evening remembrance.
Read daily life receiving a dewdrop of bounty.
shortened: It befits the divine friends to receive in every breath a dewdrop from the eternal bounty and take their share from the remembrance of God, so that they may bring their days to an end with the utmost joy and delight.

order.why: Hear the prayer for melodies that gladden the friends.
Consider praise and music as expressions of delight.
shortened: In any case, always warble in the garden of divine knowledge with various melodies and novel tunes in praise of this servant's servitude, that the spirit may be stirred, the heart gladdened, the soul may find joy and delight, the lights of happiness may shine forth, and the bounty of joy may increase.

order.why: Read the prayer’s imagery of fragrances, pearls, and song.
Keep the invitation to a melody reaching the realm above.
shortened: Be joyous, be happy, and out of the intensity of gladness and delight, raise such a melody and song that the ancient Persians will be moved to ecstasy and joy in the realm above.

order.why: Read laughter itself within the language of devotion.
shortened: Thou must show such joy and gladness, and seek such delight and felicity, that thy laughter of joy and bliss may reach the Kingdom of the All-Forgiving Lord.

order.why: Hear the call to singing and gratitude in its available wording.
Consider one person’s song stirring gladness in others.
Read patience, remembrance, and the influence of shared joy.
Connect the leaping heart with servitude.
shortened: Hold ye fast to the hem of God's garment, and direct all your efforts toward furthering His Covenant, and burning ever more brightly with the fire of His love, that your hearts may leap for joy in the breathings of servitude which well out from the breast of Abdu'l-Baha.

order.why: Join merry rejoicing with meekness and purity.
shortened: Let God's beloved, each and every one, be the essence of purity, the very life of holiness, so that in every country they may become famed for their sanctity, independence of spirit, and meekness. Let them be cheered by draughts from the eternal cup of love for God, and make merry as they drink from the wine-vaults of Heaven.

order.why: Read joy among the qualities of those who assist the Covenant.
shortened: "Ye are the angels, if your feet be firm, your spirits rejoiced, your secret thoughts pure, your eyes consoled, your ears opened, your breasts dilated with joy, and your souls gladdened, and if you arise to assist the Covenant, to resist dissension and to be attracted to the Effulgence!

order.why: Keep the particular contrast between friends and ill-wishers in its source context.
shortened: The friends are in the utmost joy and delight while the ill-wishers are disappointed, condemned and rejected.

order.why: Read the happiness of a gathered community.
shortened: Tonight I am in the greatest happiness, looking upon this concourse of God. Your meeting here is surely an evidence that you are upholding the Cause of God, that you are aiding and assisting in establishing the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Consider present fellowship and the hope of reunion.
Read another person’s joy as a source of one’s own happiness.
shortened: To see the joy of divine gladness on your faces is the cause of my happiness, for when I see you happy, I am happy also. The divine messengers come to bring joy to this earth, for this is the planet of tribulation and torment and the mission of the great masters is to turn men away from these anxieties and to infuse life with infinite joy.

order.why: Consider remembrance of friends as a source of delight.
shortened: The greatest means of joy and gladness is the mention of the divine friends.
This will cause enthusiasm and rapture in the friends and attraction and delight in the loved ones.

order.why: Read the recalled conversation that brought unexpected gladness.
Consider the wish for letters that gladden hearts.
Read the reported counsel to share good tidings.
shortened: Be ye always the bearers of good tidings and spread such news quickly, and become the means through which the hearts are made cheerful and vigilant.

order.why: Carry glad tidings outward from a visit.
shortened: Therefore when you go back from here you must go with perfect joy and give the glad tidings to every one.

order.why: Consider the consoling effect of a cheerful countenance.
Read the image of a child responding to another person’s face.
shortened: A bright and happy face cheers people on their way. If you are sad, and pass a child who is laughing, the child, seeing your sad face, will cease to laugh, not knowing why. If the day be dark, how much a gleam of sunshine is prized; so let believers wear smiling happy faces, gleaming like sunshine in the darkness.

order.why: Keep the connection between inward glad tidings and outward expression.
shortened: That we must always have a cheerful face because of the glad tidings in our hearts.

order.why: Read the invitation to radiance among people.
shortened: Be ye among the servants with joy and radiance such that the gladness of paradise may be perceived in your faces.

order.why: Consider making hearts joyful as a continuing effort.
Connect joy with mercy, charity, and refusal to dwell on faults.
shortened: Live in such a way that when people observe your manners, morals and conduct they may exclaim, 'These are not men and women, but angels of the Lord.' Be ye kind to all mankind. Let mercy be the motive power in your dealings with people. Do not look at their shortcomings. Win the hearts through love and charity; set them aglow with the fire of the love of God. The joy of a soul is indescribable, if the fragrance of spirituality waft from the garden of his being. This diving happiness is not followed by any sorrow nor is this heavenly spring ended by the sultry days of summer.

order.why: Read the forceful summons to serve humanity amid its failings.
shortened: This world of man is now an arena for wild beasts, a field where the ignorant, the heedless, seize their chance. The souls of men are ravening wolves and animals with blinded eyes, they are either deadly poison or useless weeds -- all except for a very few who indeed do nurture altruistic aims and plans for the well-being of their fellow men: but ye must in this matter -- that is, the serving of humankind -- lay down your very lives, and as ye yield yourselves, rejoice.

order.why: Consider becoming heralds of happiness through one’s influence.
Keep the reported relation between happiness and spiritual growth in its source voice.
Read the report’s emphatic association of happiness and spiritual life.
Keep the reported description of happiness as an attribute of a Baha’i.
Consider the call to avoid misanthropy and pessimism.
Hear the concise reported summons to gladness.
shortened: One must always be joyous, must always be radiant, must always be filled with gladness.

order.why: Retain the brief conclusion about rejoicing in its own source.
shortened: They sow their seed in firm ground. They write upon the surface of iron and steel. That is when they father many harvests and their writings bestow eternal significances. Therefore they must be in the utmost happiness and rejoicing.

order.why: Read enjoyment of blessings alongside the warning about empty praise.
shortened: If a man does not do these things, even though he praises God and offers him a hundred thousand thanksgivings every second there will be for that man not the slightest result; it will be but words without light. Consequently, we must be very happy, very glad, very much pleased, very contented, very joyful, because we are submerged in the ocean of the bestowals of Baha'u'llah...	A thoughtful man enjoys the gifts and the blessings of God.

order.why: Consider the story’s association of delight with character.
shortened: I saw that all these things he spoke of held absolutely no importance for the woman. Her thought was that the desert was good and she was in the utmost joy. Human joy, comfort and delight depend on character.

order.why: Keep the reported conclusion concerning a good man’s life.
shortened: The believers asked him several times to call on the Blessed Perfection but he would flatly refuse while saying:- 'How can I, the essence of sin stand in the Presence of the essence of Holiness! I am not worthy of this privilege! Whenever I find that I have attained to this merit I will go but not now, not now.' Thus this good man lived and died in happiness.

order.why: Read the effort to live joyfully through spiritual commitment.
Consider the reported connection with self-abnegation and bestowals.
Read the report’s account of spiritual happiness embracing material happiness.
Keep the reported daily provision for happiness in its source setting.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty said, 'In every twenty-four hours, two hours must be spent in a way that will cause happiness.'

order.why: Hear the concise blessing.
Conclude the linked readings with courage, discernment, and steadfast knowledge.
shortened: Happy are the righteous that have attained unto the most great truth; happy are the wise that have recognized the straight path of God and turned unto His Kingdom; happy are the glad and sincere, the lamps of whose hearts burn with the knowledge of the All-Merciful  and are protected by self-abnegation from the rough winds of test and sorrows; happy are the brave whose hearts the power of the oppressor cannot daunt; happy are the clearsighted that have learned to distinguish the transitory from the eternal, that have turned their faces to the Imperishable and are named among the Immortals in the realm of power and glory.

order.why: Read the supplied translation on two kinds of happiness in its own wording.
Follow study and spiritual focus into action, retaining the supplied opening omission.
Consider the Bab’s supplied counsels on aspiration, truthfulness, and reciprocity.
Read the distinction between balanced humor and empty diversion.
shortened: Abandonment of "a frivolous conduct" does not imply that a Baha'i must be sour-faced or perpetually solemn. Humour, happiness, joy are characteristics of a true Baha'i life. Frivolity palls and eventually leads to boredom and emptiness, but true happiness and joy and humour that are parts of a balanced life that includes serious thought, compassion and humble servitude to God are characteristics that enrich life and add to its radiance.

order.why: Close with the joy of bringing hope to another heart.

questions: What does the scene of tea in a meadow suggest about attention, gratitude, and contentment?
How do these readings relate inward happiness to the practical well-being of other people?
What do the ocean, candle, garden, and star images help us understand about joy through changing circumstances?
How does the Dhammapada’s account of happiness without hostility compare with the devotional and ethical sources of joy described here?
How might invitations to rejoice be offered with tenderness to someone experiencing grief or hardship?
What practices of fellowship, humor, service, or remembrance could help joy become something shared?
