references.note: Read the opening verses of chapter XV: happiness free of hostility amid hostile surroundings, joy without possessions, and ease beyond winning and losing. Compare this Buddhist account with the compilation’s images of inward freedom, its devotional grounding in divine love, and its practical concern for bringing joy to others.

subjects.displayTitle: Words and deeds: giving belief a visible life
subjects.introduction: Knowing that ten thousand people are cold and hungry does nothing for any of them, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá remarks, unless someone feeds and clothes them. That plain test runs through everything Bahá’u’lláh teaches about belief: words without deeds are bees that yield no honey, trees that bear no fruit, medicine the patient recognises and never takes. A thousand loads of talk about zeal and generosity are not worth a penny beside one small act. Gentle words quench thirst when they rise from a life of integrity, and when word and deed agree the effect is light upon light. What it refuses is the substitution of one for the other, offering a daily practice instead: compare your conduct with the teachings, give thanks where they agree, seek forgiveness where they do not. James, asking what use it is to wish a hungry person warmth, presses the same point. From here the way leads toward goodly deeds and service to others, toward silence and fewness of words, and toward the power of speech when something lived stands behind it.
subjects.arc: Begin with tangible help and the difficulty of practice, explore deeds as evidence of love and faith, recover the partnership of speech and action, and move toward reflection, service, and persistent effort.

order.why: Join the test of conduct with the effect of gentle speech.
shortened: O people! Words must be supported by deeds, for deeds are the true test of words. Without the former, the latter can never quench the thirst of the yearning soul, nor unlock the portals of vision before the eyes of the blind. The Lord of celestial wisdom saith: A harsh word is even as a sword thrust; a gentle word as milk. The latter leadeth the children of men unto knowledge and conferreth upon them true distinction.

order.why: Open with the needs of cold and hungry people and the road that must be walked.
Make love concrete through visiting and consoling a friend.
shortened: Go to see each other and be consoling friends to all. If a friend lives a little distance from the town, go to see him. Do not content yourselves with words only but act according to the commandments of God.

order.why: Contrast a small deed with an abundance of claims.
shortened: Look at the deeds, what concern have you with words? A thousand loads of words about zeal, enthusiasm, magnanimity, protection and chivalry are not worth a penny, but one small deed is worth a flowing treasure.

order.why: Acknowledge the difficulty of practicing what is easy to hear.
Introduce the greater power of congruent words and deeds.
Follow knowledge through resolve to action.
shortened: We cannot bring Love and Unity to pass only by talk. Knowledge is not enough. Wealth, science, education are good, we know that, but we must also work and study.
Knowledge is the first step; Resolve, the second step; Action, the fulfillment, is the third step.

order.why: Make comparison with the teachings a practice of gratitude and correction.
Read the Hidden Words’ call to distinguish oneself by deeds.
Consider human existence as a tree known through its fruits.
Read the bees and fruitless trees in their concise form.
shortened: Words must be followed by deeds; words without deeds are as bees that yield no honey, as trees that bear no fruit.

order.why: Explore the same images through the particular critique of the Sage of Sabzivar.
Join knowing and acting through the fruits of existence.
Consider attention to hearts, meanings, and sound purposes beyond eloquent phrases.
shortened: Words and phrases held no authority - novel meanings and sound purposes were accepted and beloved. They looked to hearts, not inscriptions. They listened to the secrets of the heart, not the cryptic words of eloquent writers.

order.why: Read conduct as the measure of human quality.
shortened: O Ghulam-Rida! Consider man as a sword: while it remains in its sheath, its quality remains hidden and concealed. Through God's grace, you must be freed from the sheath of darkness, that your quality may become manifest to all the world. The quality of man lies in his conduct and deeds.

order.why: Consider claims as dependent on deeds.
Read actions as the witness that words require.
Keep the parallel distinction between conjecture and certainty.
shortened: Conjecture cannot take the place of certainty, nor can words stand in lieu of deeds.

order.why: Hear the brief statement of correspondence.
Keep the companion statement in its own source.
Read manner, conduct, deeds, and words together.
Consider sincerity, certitude, faith, and knowledge as requiring action.
Read faith as more than verbal profession.
shortened: Faith in God consisteth not in words alone - deeds are required.

order.why: Consider recognition and observance as inseparable duties.
shortened: The first duty prescribed by God for His servants is the recognition of Him Who is the Dayspring of His Revelation and the Fountain of His laws, Who representeth the Godhead in both the Kingdom of His Cause and the world of creation. Whoso achieveth this duty hath attained unto all good; and whoso is deprived thereof hath gone astray, though he be the author of every righteous deed. It behoveth every one who reacheth this most sublime station, this summit of transcendent glory, to observe every ordinance of Him Who is the Desire of the world. These twin duties are inseparable. Neither is acceptable without the other.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of recognition and acceptance explicit.
Read the companion statement linking deeds with recognition.
shortened: Today all deeds and stations depend upon the recognition of God and acceptance of Him.

order.why: Consider the Bab’s warning that sought-for recognition might be refused when offered.
Read the challenge of contradiction between profession and response to revelation.
shortened: Should your words, O people, be at variance with your deeds, what then shall distinguish you from those who profess their faith in the Lord, their God, and yet, when He came down to them overshadowed with clouds, rejected Him and waxed proud before God, the Incomparable, the Omniscient?

order.why: Consider the need for evidence beyond claims of attachment.
Read the communal consequences attributed to neglect of revealed deeds.
shortened: Many are those who verbally acknowledge the appearance of Truth and His power, yet since they have not held fast to the deeds that were revealed in God's Book, they have become the cause of delay for the people of earth.

order.why: Read the challenge to fasting and prayer without the conduct they require.
Ask what makes worship fruitful in the source’s account.
Read merit through action according to the Book.
shortened: Merit lies not with those who make verbal profession, but rather with those who act according to what the All-Merciful hath revealed in His wondrous Book.

order.why: Consider the motive of acting purely for God.
shortened: Words are not accepted, but rather deeds performed purely for God, the One, the Almighty, the Glorious, the Most High.

order.why: Read even one word as a seed when it becomes a deed for God.
shortened: Praise be to God that you have been blessed with the bounty of health, which is the greatest of divine bounties. God willing, you will be assisted in that which befitteth this divine Day, for any deed that appeareth today purely for the sake of God, even if it be but a single word, is like unto a seed deposited in pure, good and blessed soil - it will surely bring forth lofty and wondrous ears of corn. Today is the day of sowing and planting, today is the day of planting trees.

order.why: Keep the pairing of a word and a pure deed with its source omission.
Consider their transforming power in this concise image.
shortened: Time and again this word has flowed from the Pen: through one word and one pure deed, the earth has transcended the heavens.

order.why: Read the earth as a record of words and deeds.
Consider a good deed as a teacher.
shortened: Say: Today befitting deeds and pleasing words are needed. Every goodly deed is in itself a teacher of the Cause.

order.why: Join spiritual attributes, clear speech, and a happy face in teaching.
shortened: As to the fundamentals of teaching the Faith: know thou that delivering the Message can be accomplished only through goodly deeds and spiritual attributes, an utterance that is crystal clear and the happiness reflected from the face of that one who is expounding the Teachings. It is essential that the deeds of the teacher should attest the truth of his words.

order.why: Read action preparing a thirst for the spoken message.
Compare education by words and education by deeds.
shortened: Furthermore, the power of teaching and education is of two kinds: One is that through words humans educate souls, the other is that through deeds humans educate. It is possible to educate people through words, but greater than that is education through deeds, for deeds have more effect.

order.why: Consider several forms of counsel while questioning words as a sufficient criterion.
shortened: O mindful rememberer! Exhortations and counsels are sometimes given through words, and sometimes through deeds and actions, through spiritual fragrances and pre-dawn prayers. However, mere words have never been and are not the criterion of truth and evidence of awakening and insight.

order.why: Read the need for an expounder alongside written proofs.
shortened: Although books and treatises of proofs are a means of awakening souls, an expounder is needed. Mere books of proofs will not cause complete propagation.

order.why: Keep the explicit call to speak and reason as well as show good conduct.
Read the question about speech and writing together with the answer about action.
Hear the hope for success in both forms of teaching.
shortened: Teaching the Cause of God is of two kinds: by word and by deed. I hope you will be successful in both.

order.why: Keep word conjoined with deed.
shortened: You must give the message through action and deed, not alone by word. Word must be conjoined with deed.

order.why: Read conduct and speech as expressions of belief.
shortened: Spread the divine fragrances and to exemplify your beliefs with your conduct and your behaviour as well as your words.

order.why: Consider words as proof and deeds as evidence of love.
shortened: Strive to conduct yourself among people such that your words become a decisive proof and your deeds evidence of love for the Brilliant Luminary.

order.why: Read congruence as light upon light, retaining the source omission.
Join speech, conduct, and character in teaching.
Place that combination within a wider account of faithfulness.
shortened: Convey to each and every one of the friends the Most Glorious, Most Wondrous greetings, and tell them that among the proofs of faithfulness to the Holy Threshold of the Blessed Beauty is that in all things - that is, in speech and conduct and deeds, in sanctification and detachment and unity and harmony, in the fear of God and righteousness - you should promote the Cause of God and engage in service, so that you may become manifest signs of the King of Oneness.

order.why: Consider the same correspondence in an assembly’s life.
Read the hoped-for community whose deeds and words awaken others.
Consider the influence of a single sanctified deed.
shortened: The people of Baha must spread the divine fragrances through deeds more than words, for a single deed emanating from the essence of sanctity will promote the Cause such that its fragrant breezes will spread to all regions.

order.why: Read wise action in a particular city’s circumstances.
shortened: Now in that city bereft (of spiritual bounties), one must act with wisdom and awaken the heedless through Baha'i deeds, for deeds have more influence than words.

order.why: Keep the call to acquire spiritual characteristics.
Read kindness, sympathy, and trustworthiness before the final mention of speech.
shortened: Teaching the cause of God is not only through the tongue; it is through deeds, a good disposition, happiness of nature, kindness, sympathy, good fellowship, trustworthiness, holiness, virtue, purity of ideals and lastly, speech.

order.why: Consider the public testimony of disinterested and universal aims.
shortened: The believers must teach the Cause not only in words but must adorn themselves with the ornaments of deeds in order that all mankind may bear testimony to this, that their aims are universal, their actions disinterested, their purposes inspiring and all-embracing, so that they may witness in their behavior and manner the holiness, purity, sincerity and loving kindness of the prophets of God… Tell them to read carefully the Persian and Arabic 'Hidden Words' and to live and behave according to their contents.

order.why: Follow living the message into raising the downtrodden.
shortened: Thus in teaching the Cause it is not sufficient to give the message, we must live it, work for it, be attracted to it, enkindle others with its fire, perfume the nostrils with its fragrance, surround our companions with its atmosphere, impress mankind with its grandeur and loftiness and raise the lowly and downtrodden to the highest pinnacle of honor and glory.

order.why: Read love extending across religions and races through deeds.
shortened: Love ye all religions and all races with a love that is true and sincere and show that love through deeds and not through the tongue; for the latter hath no importance, as the majority of men are, in speech, well-wishers, while action is the best.

order.why: Keep service to people of any belief explicit.
Consider kindness and care replacing predatory conduct.
Ask what remedies a merely verbal fellowship.
Read the difficulty of benevolence in action.
Distinguish speaking of generosity, justice, or light from embodying them.
shortened: Consider the difference between one who speaks of generosity and the one who is generous; between the one who claims justice and equity, and the one who is just and equitable. Or how significant is the contrast between the one who speaks of light, and the one who is illumined. If we were to follow the teachings and dictums of the Blessed Beauty, even stones and plants would be affected.

order.why: Consider love recognized through conduct rather than repeated assertion.
shortened: The world is wrong, just because people talk too much and do not carry out their ideals. If action took the place of words, the world would change very soon. A man who does good and does not talk about it is perfect. The man who does very little good and magnifies it in his speech, is not good. if I love you, you know it, I need not tell you all the time; on the other hand, if I did not love you, you would know it also, and you would not believe me if I said I did love you a thousand times.

order.why: Read the concrete test of whether hearers receive material assistance.
shortened: If you give them only words, when they put their hands into their pockets after you have gone, they will find themselves none the richer for you!"

order.why: Move from wishing to do good toward acting.
Read unity as something requiring work.
shortened: Unity is good. To know this is not sufficient. You must intend to promote it, you must work for it. Knowledge is a good thing, but it is only the first step. If knowledge is alone it is stationary. These meetings teach us that Unity is good, and that suppression (slavery under the yoke of traditions and prejudices) is the cause of disunion. To know this is not enough. All knowledge is good, but it can bear no fruit but by action. It is well to know that riches are good, but that knowledge will not make a man rich; he must work, he must put his knowledge into practice.

order.why: Follow knowledge of light into receiving and reflecting it.
Consider the medicine that must be used.
Read the companion physician analogy and the call to compare conduct.
shortened: They recognize the Physician. Now they must act according to the teachings of Baha'u'llah. They must use the medicine appointed by the Real Physician. They have to compare their actions with the teachings so that all the people may witness and bear record that these people are real Bahais. A sick person knows the physician and received the medicine, but when he does not use it, what is the use of it?

order.why: Follow chanting through pondering into action.
Ask what it means to read and praise a Tablet without practicing it.
shortened: O divine friends! These counsels and exhortations of the Blessed Beauty have been revealed from the Supreme Pen so that they may be acted upon, not merely read. Many souls read these Tablets and praise them but do not act according to a single word.

order.why: Consider the reported picture of letters read and stored away.
shortened: The friends are waiting each day for a new letter to reach them from me. And after receiving it, they read it and put it in their boxes and again wait for another letter, which they will again read and preserve in a box.

order.why: Read the distinction between reading and attempting to live.
shortened: Abdul-Baha: Live thou in accord with the teachings of Baha'u'llah. Do not only read them. There is a vast difference between the soul who merely reads the words of Baha'u'llah and the one who tries to live them.

order.why: Consider remembering the teachings at the moment of action.
Hear the direct challenge to agreement without practice.
Read recitation in relation to results.
shortened: Today is the day of deeds. If we content ourselves with merely reciting what is in the divine scriptures, it will never yield results. Therefore we must strive with heart and soul to become successful in action.

order.why: Connect progress with practice.
Keep conduct necessary beyond stories and good intention.
shortened: O friends! This mighty cycle is the cycle of lights and the age of mysteries and the century of effects. It cannot be completed through stories and narratives, nor accomplished through pure intention alone. Deeds are needed, conduct is required, divine counsels and admonitions must be carried out.

order.why: Read the invitation to enter the field rather than only hear its stories.
Consider receiving nourishment before sharing it.
shortened: These days are the days of Faith and Deeds-not the days of words and lip service:  Let us arise from the sleep of negligence, and realize what a great feast is prepared for us; first eating thereof ourselves, then giving unto others who are thirsting for the Water of Knowledge, and hungering for the Bread of Life.

order.why: Read gratitude expressed through action.
shortened: There is a cordial thanksgiving, too, which expresses itself in the deeds and actions of man when his heart is filled with gratitude. For example, God has conferred upon man the gift of guidance, and in thankfulness for this great gift certain deeds must emanate from him. To express his gratitude for the favors of God man must show forth praiseworthy actions.

order.why: Keep thanksgiving through deeds in the letter to western communities.
shortened: Deliver on my behalf divine glad-tidings to the assembles in Seattle, the members of the houses of Mrs... and Mrs... and the assemblies in Portland and Denver and say: "O ye sons and daughters of the Kingdom! Be ye thankful that although the light of guidance hath dawned from the East, yet, praise be to God, it illuminated both the East and the West! In order that glorification and thanks may be shown for these bounties, the word and actions must be in accordance with the advices and behests of His Highness Baha'u'llah. Thanks does not depend upon words but upon deeds!"

order.why: Consider the warning about praise without the conduct it requires.
shortened: If a man does not do these things, even though he praises God and offers him a hundred thousand thanksgivings every second there will be for that man not the slightest result; it will be but words without light.

order.why: Read the sun’s rising as a summons to work.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty endured all these afflictions and tribulations so that we might succeed in deeds, not just in words. The sun rises so that people might engage in work, not engage in talk. The Sun of Truth likewise rises so that souls might succeed in deeds, not just in words. "Bring forth deeds if thou art truthful," not "Bring forth words if thou art truthful."

order.why: Consider the report’s contrasting accounts of a day spent.
Read the comparison between attending to duties and boasting.
Consider action without publicizing one’s virtue.
shortened: People do much speaking to advance their own glory and to make themselves appear superior to their neighbors. But if you do the Will of God and do not blazon it abroad, then you will change the whole world. They who do most speak least.

order.why: Read conventional language of sacrifice as distinct from actual sacrifice.
Consider the time of trial as the test of a promise.
Read the particular criticism of a ruler’s unfulfilled assurance.
Keep the contradiction between preaching peace and killing starkly visible.
Read the report’s critique of Christian profession as a particular religious argument.
Consider the reported appeal to the Gospel in the discussion of livelihood and preaching.
shortened: Have they faith enough to work and preach and not receive any large salary? If they have made up their minds to walk in the footsteps of Christ and his apostles, this is the path. "Read Matt. Chapter 6. V. 24/34.) If they do not live according to these clear injunctions, all the lectures, articles and talks will bring to result. "Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the Kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven."

order.why: Read the Qur’anic allusion to verbal belief.
Consider the reference to Christ’s image of fruits.
Read that image in relation to divine qualities.
shortened: Christ said, "Ye shall know them by their fruits" - the qualities of a believer show what kind of believer he is. If a man claims to be a believer and does not show forth the qualities of God, it proves that he is a believer in name only, and that he has not yet been regenerated by the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Ask how actions disclose the condition of spiritual life.
Consider the distinction between a religious name and lived attributes.
shortened: A person may claim to be a Baha'i or may be known as a Baha'i for all his life and may not know at all what a Baha'i means. Another person may never have heard the name Baha'i and may at the same time practice all the attributes which are necessary to make one a Baha'i. That is why his holiness Christ says, those who are not against us are with us. You must know the tree by its fruits.

order.why: Keep the related reported answer in its own wording.
shortened: "It makes no difference whether you have ever heard of Baha'u'llah or not," was the answer, "the man who lives the life according to the teachings of Baha'u'llah is already a Baha'i. On the other hand a man may call himself a Baha'i for fifty years and if he does not live the life he is not a Baha'i.

order.why: Read the explicit comparison of good conduct without professed belief and corrupt conduct with it.
shortened: Undoubtedly, a person, who is not a believer, but whose deeds and morals are good, is far better than one who claims his belief in words but, who, in actions, is a follower of satan.

order.why: Keep the reported priority given to deeds over claims.
shortened: The point of distinction among men, let them remember, is their deeds, not their beliefs or words.

order.why: Follow professed belief toward wisdom and the betterment of all.
Read the report’s account of belief as praiseworthy qualities and acts.
Consider becoming an embodiment of teachings.
shortened: And with perfect severance, spirituality and the best intent and effort must they hasten to promulgate the Divine Teaching, and above all they must act according to the precepts and exhortations of His Holiness Baha'u'llah, for in this cycle of Baha'u'llah verbal confessions and acknowledgements, literal faith and certainty and external relations are of no avail. Nay, rather, the beloved of God and the maid-servants of the Merciful must manifest such attributes and ethical conduct as to embody and personify the teachings of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Read the same responsibility in children’s education.
shortened: There is no doubt that it will yield the desired results; especially is this true of instruction as to Baha'i obligations and Baha'i conduct, for the little children must needs be made aware in their very heart and soul that "Baha'i" is not just a name but a truth. Every child must be trained in the things of the spirit, so that he may embody all the virtues and become a source of glory to the Cause of God. Otherwise, the mere word "Baha'i", if it yield no fruit, will come to nothing.

order.why: Hear the counsel to two women concerning profession and conduct.
shortened: O ye two well-loved handmaids of God! Whatever a man's tongue speaketh, that let him prove by his deeds. If he claimeth to be a believer, then let him act in accordance with the precepts of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the concise criterion of agreement between words and deeds.
shortened: He whose deeds do not accord with his words is not a true Baha'i. That is, a non-Baha'i who leads a good life does less harm to the Cause than a Baha'i whose life is not righteous.

order.why: Consider putting even one teaching into practice.
shortened: I declare by Him beside Whom there is naught else if we live in accord with one of the Teachings we will become radiant like unto this lamp. If we confess verbally that the principles of Baha'u'llah are the cause of eternal salvation and the means of nearness unto the throne of God and yet do not live according to their contents we would not be Baha'is.

order.why: Read the reputation formed through actions in one’s city.
Consider conduct as guidance to others.
shortened: Say: Beware, O people of Bahá, lest ye walk in the ways of them whose words differ from their deeds. Strive that ye may be enabled to manifest to the peoples of the earth the signs of God, and to mirror forth His commandments. Let your acts be a guide unto all mankind, for the professions of most men, be they high or low, differ from their conduct. It is through your deeds that ye can distinguish yourselves from others.

order.why: Read the request for actions that testify to relationship with truth.
shortened: Say: O friends! Words alone have not sufficed and will never suffice. You must manifest such deeds that all souls will testify that you are distinguished from others and are truly related to the Truth.

order.why: Consider the influence of pure deeds upon hearts and minds.
Read the relationship of figurative words to enacted reality.
Keep steadfastness in the Covenant connected with conduct.
shortened: Today the friends of God must strive to remain firm in the Covenant, and this cannot be accomplished through words alone - deeds and conduct are required.

order.why: Read deeds as testimony to love, detachment, and service.
shortened: Today is the day of deeds and not of words, and their deeds are a truthful witness and faithful testimony to their love, detachment and service.

order.why: Defines deeds as the witness and testimony to words.
Consider the signs attributed to ancestors’ words and conduct.
Hear the concise aspiration for deeds that confer glory.
Read the direction of words and deeds toward a common purpose.
shortened: Then all his words and deeds will tend toward the glorification of the Cause and the promotion of the Principles.

order.why: Consider the results sought from a spiritual call.
shortened: That which is truly spiritual must light the path to God, and must result in deeds. We cannot believe the call to be spiritual when there is no result.

order.why: Read the reported examples of knowledge, effort, and returning good for evil.
shortened: Every effort must have its result, else it is not a true effort. You must become the means of lighting the world of humanity. This is the infallible proof and sign. Every progress depends on two things, knowledge and practice. First acquire knowledge, and, when conviction is reached, put it into practice.
"After a little I went over and took his arm, saying, 'But you must return good for evil. Whether I honoured you or despised you, you should follow the teachings; now you merely read them.

order.why: Keep the report of teaching by example and its source omission.
Read the aspiration for deeds to exceed words in the service of humanity.
Hear the concise assessment of lived example.
Read deeds followed by wisdom and utterance.
shortened: In previous cycles and past centuries, teaching was done through words, but in this time it is through deeds.

One must first teach through deeds and afterwards through wisdom and utterance, and show heartfelt kindness to all peoples and nations, for they say "The effect of deeds is more penetrating than the effect of words." Souls are weary of words but attentive to deeds.

order.why: Consider the source’s insistence on actions confirming claims.
shortened: But all these sayings are but words and we see very few of them carried into the world of action.
They must on all occasions confirm by their actions what they proclaim in words. Their deeds must prove their fidelity, and their actions must show forth Divine light.

order.why: Read the reported demand to translate utterances into life.
shortened: The utterances of Baha'u'llah are to be translated into deeds, not words (only). Deeds are demanded by His teaching, which must thus appear transmuted into the life of this day. Words are nothing.

order.why: Keep the concise reported measure of a person’s deeds.
Retain the brief call to prove through action.
Read the comparison with an earlier religious cycle as the report’s claim.
shortened: This cycle is not the cycle of words. In the Islamic cycle they would say 'There is no god but God' and that was all. This is the cycle of deeds. One must testify through deeds, not by tongue.

order.why: Keep the related reported call for deeds in this century.
shortened: For this is the Radiant Century, the time when deeds must take the place of words.

order.why: Hear the repeated emphasis on action.
shortened: O dear one! This Dispensation of the Beauty of Abha is the time of deeds, not words. The purpose is not words, but deeds!

order.why: Consider the image of the carpet of deeds rolled away.
Read the summons to act instead of waiting.
Keep the concise declaration of the day of deeds.
shortened: Today is the day of deeds, not words.

order.why: Consider actions appearing through every limb.
Read the enduring distinction attributed to a good deed.
Hear the warning against satisfaction with utterance alone.
Keep the call for actions that lead toward rest.
shortened: Verily words cannot take the place of deeds. Hold fast unto goodly and pleasing actions, and purify yourselves from the defilement of divine prohibitions that ye may attain unto true rest.

order.why: Read the counsel about whose example to follow.
shortened: Say: O My loved ones! Hold fast unto goodly deeds and follow not those who hold fast unto words rather than deeds. These, verily, are among the heedless.

order.why: Consider the warning about abandoning deeds.
shortened: Beware lest thou be of those who have cast the deeds behind their backs and clung to mere words.

order.why: Retain the source’s severe counsel concerning empty profession.
shortened: Shun those in whom thou findest words without deeds - they are among the contemptible ones.

order.why: Read its severe contrast as rhetorical insistence on practice.
Close the linked readings with the Words of Wisdom’s emphatic demand for abundant deeds.
shortened:
The essence of faith is fewness of words and abundance
of deeds; he whose words exceed his deeds, know verily his
death is better than his life.

order.why: Read the supplied call for love and action.
Consider example, prayer, and kindness with the supplied omission visible.
Read noble conduct as testimony to the teachings.
shortened: It is primarily through the potency of noble deeds and character, rather than by the power of exposition and proofs, that the friends of God should demonstrate to the world that what has been promised by God is bound to happen, that it is already taking place and that the divine glad-tidings are clear, evident and complete.

However, if the friends become embodiments of virtue and good character, words and arguments will be superfluous. Their very deeds will well serve as eloquent testimony, and their noble conduct will ensure the preservation, integrity and glory of the Cause of God.

order.why: Follow study through meditation and prayer into persevering action.
shortened: The beloved Guardian has stressed over and over again, that to effectively teach the Faith, the individual must study deeply, the Divine Word, imbibe Its life-giving waters, and feast upon Its glorious teachings. He should then meditate on the import of the Word, and finding its spiritual depths, pray for guidance and assistance. But most important, after prayer is action. After one has prayed and meditated, he must arise, relying fully on the guidance and confirmation of Baha'u'llah, to teach His Faith. Perseverance in action is essential, just as wisdom and audacity are necessary for effective teaching.

order.why: Make room for learning through imperfect attempts at action.
Keep the supplied statement about belief becoming effective.
Close by considering the spirit of wholehearted service expressed through acts.

questions: What practical tests do these readings offer for the sincerity of love, generosity, and faith?
Why is it often easier to understand or praise a teaching than to act on it?
When do speech and action strengthen one another, and when does speech become a substitute for action?
How does James’s example of a person needing food and clothing illuminate the relationship between faith and care?
What might honest comparison of one’s conduct with one’s convictions involve, without becoming a judgment of other people?
How can prayer, reflection, and willingness to learn from imperfect action support a more consistent life of service?

references.label: 1 · James 2:14–18 · Faith and concrete care
references.note: Read the challenge about offering comforting words to someone lacking clothing and food while leaving those needs unmet. James connects the visibility of faith with works. Compare that argument with the compilation’s call to translate love and knowledge into service, and with its account of speech and action reinforcing one another.

subjects.displayTitle: Tree of life: shelter, revelation, and shared growth
subjects.introduction: The Lote Tree beyond which there is no passing stands in the Qur’án at the boundary of a journey, near the Garden of Refuge; Bahá’u’lláh takes the same name and makes the Tree speak. From its leaves comes the summons that there is no God but God, from its branches the warbling of the Dove, and in its fire the voice Moses heard in the Bush that was not consumed. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains the image directly: the Tree of Life is the Word of God and His universal Manifestation, the root that does not itself bear fruit but feeds the branches that do. Its shade falls over East and West alike. Its fruit is everlasting life, its leaves, like those in John’s Revelation, are for the healing of nations, and the men and women who grow from it are themselves addressed as branches and leaves, called to stay green in every season. The journey continues through the other names the Manifestation bears, the divine physician and the educator, the gardener who plants, the pen that writes and the sun that lights every mirror.
subjects.arc: Begin with shared shelter and living fruit, explore the Tree as an image of revelation, follow its scriptural echoes and summons, then consider the growth, care, and conduct of its branches and leaves.

order.why: Introduce the explicit identification of the Tree with the Word and Manifestation.
Open with peoples of East and West finding fellowship beneath one shelter.
Read the Tree of Life bearing the fruits of God in the Tablet of Ahmad.
shortened: Verily He is the Tree of Life that bringeth forth the fruits of God, the Exalted, the Powerful, the Great.

order.why: Keep the qualification that Tree has this meaning in one sense.
shortened: The Holy Tree (Sadrat) is, in a sense, the Manifestation of the One True God, exalted be He. The Blessed Tree in the land of Za'faran refereth to the land which is flourishing, blessed, holy and all-perfumed, where that Tree hath been planted.

order.why: Explore the Word appearing in the images of human being, light, tree, and sun.
Read the interpretation of the biblical Tree and its leaves.
Consider a branch bearing fruit in every season.
Keep the reported explanation of the human Word and life in its own source.
Read the reported gathering of images from Christ, Muhammad, Moses, and Bahaullah.
Keep the reported account of root, branch, and fruit distinct from the other explanations.
Uses successive trees to explain the continuity of religious dispensations.
Read the Aqdas passage in which the sacred Tree calls from the crimson spot.
shortened: Advance, O people, with snow-white faces and radiant hearts, unto the blest and crimson Spot, wherein the Sadratu'l-Muntaha is calling: "Verily, there is none other God beside Me, the Omnipotent Protector, the Self-Subsisting!"

Give ear unto the verses of God which He Who is the sacred Lote-Tree reciteth unto you. They are assuredly the infallible balance, established by God, the Lord of this world and the next. Through them the soul of man is caused to wing its flight towards the Dayspring of Revelation, and the heart of every true believer is suffused with light.

order.why: Consider the challenge of recognizing the voice associated with the Burning Bush.
shortened: O 'Ali! That which they accepted from the Bush they now refuse to accept from Him Who is the Tree of the world of existence.

order.why: Follow the connection between the fire of Moses and the illumination of Bahaullah.
Read the name Musa and the same Caller in the human Manifestation.
Hear the Sinai, Bush, and Vineyard images together.
shortened: Verily Sinai hath been graced to behold its Speaker, the Burning Bush to know its Herald, and the Vineyard of God to see its Beloved.

order.why: Read the Speaker on the Mount in relation to scriptural promise.
shortened: O thou who gazest toward the horizon of the Revelation! Hearken unto that which the Speaker of the Mount uttereth, Who was promised in the Books of God and mentioned by the tongues of the Messengers.

order.why: Consider companions illumined through the fire of the Tree.
Join gratitude for guidance with the Sinai image.
Read hearing the Tree as a source of knowledge.
shortened: And We testify that thou didst attain unto the Station and didst hear what the Blessed Tree spoke forth from the Sinai of divine knowledge.

order.why: Keep Sinai, Paran, and Tur together in this address to a branch.
shortened: O branch extended, proceeding and raised from the Blessed Tree which was raised up in truth on the Sinai of Manifestation, the Spot of Light, the right-hand Valley, the Paran of the All-Merciful, the wilderness of Tur!

order.why: Read the concise address to a branch of Sinai.
shortened: O graceful branch of the Tree of Sinai! Blessed art thou to have sprung from this Sacred Tree and to have branched out from this Blessed Sadrih.

order.why: Consider the Tree beyond East and West within the language of holy ground.
Read the blessed Tree and light without fire in the Bab’s wording.
Keep the Bab’s account of the Tree’s origin and station in its theological terms.
Read the garden, Point, and Tree imagery with the source omission retained.
Consider the Tree and nearness imagery in the visitation for a martyred Letter of the Living.
Hear the Lord of the Flame in the Deathless Tree within the Holy Mariner.
shortened: A station wherein the Lord hath in the Flame of His Beauty appeared within the deathless tree; Glorified be my Lord, the All-Glorious!

order.why: Read hair, light, Sinai, and fire together as devotional imagery.
Consider the returning fire and the voice from the Tree.
shortened: Say: By God! The Fire hath returned in the Tree and speaketh forth: 'I am, verily, God, the Mighty, the Exalted, the Well-Beloved.'

order.why: Hear the blessed ear’s response to the light and fire.
shortened: Verily the Light calleth aloud and the Fire proclaimeth: Blessed be the ear that hath heard and hath attained unto that which God hath desired in His glorious and wondrous Day.

order.why: Read the same declaration from the blessed spot.
shortened: Hearken unto what is revealed unto thee from this Tree upon this blessed spot from this Divine Fire, that verily there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Join the light within the fire with the proclamation of divine sovereignty.
shortened: The Light hath shone forth and the Fire hath called out from the Divine Lote-Tree: "The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the Possessor of all that was and shall be."

order.why: Consider the Tree’s Planter and the fire’s Kindler in the address to the Mount.
Read communion upon the Mount and the blazing Tree.
shortened: Today the Mount is in communion with Him Who conversed with it, and the Tree beyond which there is no passing is ablaze in the luminous spot.

order.why: Keep the melodies of the Tree with the Speaker on Sinai.
Consider the human Tree and the fire that appears beyond East and West.
Read the breeze of revelation and the Remote Mosque allusion in their source setting.
Explore the promise of shelter from the heat of self and passion.
shortened: O servant who art mentioned in this inscribed Tablet! Know thou that We created the Sidrat'ul-Muntaha in the crimson hill beyond the crimson sea of grandeur, and raised it to such a station that were all who are in the heavens and on earth to seek shelter beneath one of its leaves, they would be preserved from the heat of self and passion, inasmuch as We shed upon it a light from the lights of this Sun which hath dawned in truth - thus hath the matter been decreed, if thou be of them that know.

order.why: Hear the call from the leaves and the shelter offered to all humanity.
shortened: O loved ones of God among the Arabs!  Hearken to the summons of God issuing from this Tree which hath been raised up through the power of truth, every leaf of which proclaimeth within all things:  Verily, I am God; there is no God but Him, the Most Holy, the All-Glorious, the Most Bountiful!  Hasten, O people, unto the Tree of God, and seek shelter beneath its shadow.  By the righteousness of the one true God!  Were ye to search the reaches of earth and heaven, ye would find no refuge save beneath the shade of this Tree, a Tree which overshadoweth all mankind and through whose branches waft such divine breezes as will quicken every mouldering bone.

order.why: Consider the Tree watered by life and encompassing all.
Read the extension of grace to followers of all religions.
shortened: Then give thanks unto my Lord, the Great, for this wondrous favor. This is a day wherein grace hath encompassed all religions, and the Divine Lott Tree hath called out from the Most Exalted Horizon: 'Verily, there is none other God but Him, the One, the Single, the All-Knowing.'

order.why: Keep the shared position of all beneath its shade.
Consider firm roots and branches reaching toward the Concourse on High.
Read the Tree of Paradise in relation to East and West.
Notice the varying capacity through which shelter is known.
shortened: O people! Take shelter beneath the Lote-Tree of holiness. Verily it hath been among you for numbered years, and ye have known it according to your measure and capacity. Whoso denieth it is assuredly in grievous loss.

order.why: Set the desert of deprivation beside the invitation to shade.
shortened: How many souls rushed forth into the deadly wilderness and were consumed by the heat of deprivation, never tasting a drop of the wine of reunion from the hand of the Cup-bearer of attainment, while you, through the favor of the Most Glorious Beloved, have entered beneath the sheltering shade of the Tree of the Uttermost End.

order.why: Read the counsel to avoid heedlessness and rest beneath the Tree.
Hear the leaves’ rejoicing in the invitation to detachment and shelter.
Read strangers finding shade and the thirsty finding living water.
Keep the prayer for protection and continued shelter.
shortened: Say:

O my God, my Adored One, my Desire! With utter helplessness I beseech Thee and pray fervently unto Thee to protect me from the mischief of the ungodly, and to deprive me not of the shelter of the divine Lote-Tree and of the shrill voice of the Pen of the Most High.

order.why: Hear the prayer to gather servants beneath providence.
shortened: I beseech Thee, by Thine own Self and by Him Whom Thou has appointed as the Manifestation of Thine own Being and Thy discriminating Word unto all that are in heaven and on earth, to gather together Thy servants beneath the shade of the Tree of Thy gracious providence.

order.why: Read illumination, consolation, and repose together.
shortened: If thou dost long for illumination from the Kingdom adorn thy countenance with beauty of the All-Merciful and if thou desirest consolation for thy soul and Tranquillity in thy conscience seek repose beneath the Sadratu'l-Muntaha.

order.why: Consider the act of turning toward the Most Distant Tree.
shortened: Set your faces toward the Most Distant Station - verily it is the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing, if ye be of the assured ones.

order.why: Read turning toward the Tree with a radiant heart.
Hear the concise summons to draw near.
Follow the ascent toward hearing the melodies of Paradise.
Keep the surprising image of the Tree found at the journey’s beginning.
shortened: They have traversed the Lote Tree of the utmost realm of love at the beginning of their journey and have perceived the ultimate goal of divine knowledge from the Tree of Paradise.

order.why: Read created things as fruits in the source’s image.
shortened: Verily they are the Tree beyond which there is no passing, and whatsoever is created from them are its fruits, would ye but know.

order.why: Consider a leaf and a fruit as testimony.
Read the blessings associated with its leaves, fruits, and station.
Join gifts of leaf and fruit with remembrance and nearness.
shortened: The Divine Lote-Tree desires to send unto thee a fruit from among Its fruits, and a leaf from among Its leaves, and a remembrance from among Its remembrances, that It may draw thee closer, in all conditions, to God, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.

order.why: Consider the fruit offered to raise and draw the recipient near.
Read tasting fruit beside hearing the Tree speak.
shortened: Blessed art thou for having drunk of My cup and soared in My atmosphere and tasted of the fruits of this Divine Tree which hath been raised up in truth and speaketh forth that there is none other God but Him, the Almighty, the Glorious, the Beautiful.

order.why: Keep the fruit connected with the One who planted the Tree.
shortened: And verily, thou art of the fruits of the Ultimate Tree which was planted by the hand of the Most Glorious.

order.why: Consider companionship as fruit.
Read consecration of the Tree and its fruits to God.
shortened: Consecrate Thou, O my God, the whole of this Tree unto Him, that from it may be revealed all the fruits created by God within it for Him through Whom God hath willed to reveal all that He pleaseth.

order.why: Keep the fruit of utterance within the address to humanity.
shortened: Thus hath the human one revealed the fruits of utterance from this Tree which hath been raised up in truth by God, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

order.why: Hear the Tree identified as the Word in the call to approach.
shortened: Today the Blessed Tree of Baha, which hath been planted by the hand of the Lord of Names in the Most Exalted Paradise, uttereth this most sublime Word: "O peoples of the earth! The Lord of Heaven hath come with manifest sovereignty."

order.why: Read the testimony of scriptures to the voice of the Tree.
shortened: God hath testified in His Books and Scriptures unto Him Who hath come with the Truth, with a Name through which the world was illumined and the faces of the nations were darkened, save those who held fast to the Sure Handle and turned toward the All-Highest Horizon - the Station wherein the Divine Lote-Tree doth speak: "There is none other God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting."

order.why: Consider the Ultimate Tree and Primal Word in the address to a handmaid.
Hear the call addressed to Ali-before-Nabil.
Keep the particular recipient and crimson horizon in view.
Read the call to Hasan from the green Tree.
Keep the personal address to Ahmad-i-Ali within the summons.
shortened: O Ahmad-i-'Ali, hear the Call from the Divine Lote-Tree, planted by the hands of grace in the Most Exalted Paradise.

order.why: Consider the counsel to Kuchik about holding fast and reading.
Read the Book and the sweetness of the call from the crimson Tree.
shortened: This is a Book from the Wronged One to him who hath turned towards the Crimson Tree that he might hearken unto its most sweet call in remembrance of God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Hear remembrance beside the Tree at the right of the Throne.
shortened: The Remembrance of God from the Divine Lote-Tree hath been witnessed at the right hand of the Throne. Blessed is the one who draweth nigh unto it, who is nourished by its fruits, and who taketh for himself beneath its shade a station that is faithful to the truth.

order.why: Read the Caller, heart, and Throne imagery together.
Consider the summons directed to all.
shortened: The Divine Lote-Tree crieth out amidst all beings and summoneth all unto God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Keep the concise invitation to hear the Tree.
Read the Tree’s proclamation of the Kingdom.
Hear the same proclamation in its own source.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath attained unto the Salsabil of the utterance of the All-Merciful in these days wherein the Divine Lote-Tree hath proclaimed: The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Read the Tree of Utterance addressing Ali.
Keep the invitation to turn toward the speaking Tree.
shortened: Say: Turn ye, O people, to the Supreme Horizon, the station wherein the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing doth speak.

order.why: Hear the Tree and Rock joining in the proclamation.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the Divine Lote-Tree calleth out and the Rock crieth aloud through this Great Name. Be ye as leaves when the winds of the Will of your Lord, the Lord of the Covenant, blow.

order.why: Read the Pen’s voice beside the rustling Tree.
Consider the Tree’s rustling and the Cock upon the Throne.
Read the tongue falling silent before the Tree’s declaration.
Attend to each leaf offering a different praise.
shortened: O my leaf and O my handmaiden! Today it befitteth the leaves of the Divine Lote-Tree to make mention and offer praise unto God, exalted be His glory. Each of the leaves of the Ultimate Lote-Tree is engaged in a different remembrance and uttereth a different praise.

order.why: Hear the anthem, nightingale, and invitation to the needy.
shortened: This is the garden of Paradise, wherein arise the anthems of God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting; wherein ascend the soul-entrancing melodies warbled by the Nightingale of Eternity upon the twigs of the Divine Lote-Tree; wherein abide the Maids of Heaven whom none hath touched save God, the All-Glorious, the Most Holy; and wherein lieth enshrined that which draweth the needy to the shores of the ocean of true wealth and guideth the people to the Word of God.

order.why: Read the glad tidings warbled from the branches.
shortened: She warbleth upon the twigs of the Divine Lote-Tree and giveth glad tidings unto them that are nigh and unto the sincere ones.

order.why: Keep the Dove’s continuing song in view.
shortened: O servant!
We have caused thee to hear the melodies of the Dove which warbleth at all times upon the twigs of the Divine Lote-Tree.

order.why: Join the Dove’s song with gratitude.
shortened: Thus have We sent down unto thee that which the Dove hath warbled upon the twigs of the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing, whereby all things are drawn, that thou mayest render thanks unto thy Lord and say, turning unto the Desired One: Praise be unto Thee, O Lord of existence!

order.why: Consider detachment as a way of hearing with the heart.
Read the leaves attracting the Concourse on High in the address to a handmaid.
shortened: O My handmaiden! Hearken unto My call, then detach thyself from all else besides Me, then drink from the cup of My praise from the fingers of My mercy and grandeur, then raise thy right hand in My Most Great Name and rend asunder therewith the veils of the handmaidens through My sovereignty and majesty and power and might, then hearken unto other melodies from the Divine Lote-Tree which hath been planted by the hand of Baha in the Garden of Refuge, and every leaf thereof speaketh that which attracteth the hearts of the Concourse on High.

order.why: Move from hearing the Dove to remembering others.
shortened: When thou hearest the cooing of the Dove and knowest that which the Divine Lote-Tree hath uttered, make mention of thy Lord amidst the concourse of creation, that they may haply turn toward this luminous horizon.

order.why: Join hearing through the heart with testimony through the tongue.
shortened: Hearken thou to the Call from the Divine Lote-Tree, that it may draw thee to a station wherein thou shalt testify with thy heart and tongue that there is no God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Consider fruit, remembrance, and the Pen’s inscription upon leaves.
Read hearing beside the firmly rooted Tree of grace.
shortened: Thus has the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing spoken, as a grace from its presence upon you, that ye may hear and be of those who are firmly rooted.

order.why: Hear the invitation to gratitude for listening.
Keep the brothers’ hearing and hastening in its personal setting.
shortened: Blessed be thy brother and thou, and they who have hastened with their hearts unto the Divine Lote-Tree which speaks forth in the kingdom of creation that which it spoke before creation itself: "Verily there is none other God but I, the Truth, the Mighty, the Wondrous."

order.why: Read the news carried to the loved ones.
shortened: O My loved ones in My lands! Hearken unto My call which hath been raised from the Divine Lote-Tree that speaketh amidst the world and announceth unto all this momentous News.

order.why: Follow hearing toward turning all people to God.
Read the call to the straight path.
shortened: At all times doth the Divine Lote-Tree call out betwixt earth and heaven and summon all to the straight path of God.

order.why: Consider the different responses of action and preoccupation with fancies.
Read the moving Tree and people’s heedlessness together.
shortened: The Divine Lote-Tree hath been stirred by the movement of the verses of Him Who is the Lord of all creation, yet most of the people remain heedless.

order.why: Keep the contrast between revealed verses and unheeding ears.
Consider the limits placed upon reaching the Tree without divine will.
shortened: Say: The Tree hath been raised up in truth, and the birds of the hearts of them that know cannot attain unto its heights save whom thy Lord willeth. Verily He is the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful. Blessed is he who hath heard its rustling and the warbling of the birds that circle round it.

order.why: Read the grief of an awaited Tree met with swords.
Hear the Tree’s lament and the stoning of the One offering shelter.
Keep the plea not to slay the One of whom the Dove sings.
Read the lament concerning cruelty with the source omission visible.
Hear the prayer for the growth of a Tree watered by the blood of loved ones.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O God, by the Tree which Thou hast planted at Thy affirmation and watered with the blood of Thy loved ones, to cause that Tree, its branches, leaves and fruits to grow until it reacheth that which is befitting at Thy creation and returneth to that which is worthy of the court of Thy glory and majesty.

order.why: Read the living waters beside the abiding Tree.
shortened: Strive ye that ye may quaff from the living waters and behold yourselves abiding and enduring beneath the shade of the Divine Lote-Tree in the kingdom of earth and heaven.

order.why: Consider holding fast to an enduring remembrance.
shortened: Hold thou fast in all conditions to the Divine Lote Tree, for verily it calleth out and remembereth thee at this moment with that which shall endure as long as the names of God, the Lord of all worlds, shall endure.

order.why: Keep attachment to the Tree from which the addressee has sprung.
shortened: Cling fast unto this divine Lote-Tree from which God hath graciously caused thee to spring forth.

order.why: Read the leaves of the Cause and the call to hold fast.
Hear the Tree calling its branches to steadfastness.
shortened: Verily the Divine Lote-Tree calleth out to its branches and counseleth them to remain supremely steadfast in this Cause whereby the limbs of all names have quaked.

order.why: Consider the glory addressed to steadfast branches.
Read the leaf’s perseverance amid trial.
Keep the leaf’s movement and fruit’s constancy within their devotional image.
Read the paradox of a cut branch that continues to grow and shelter the world.
Consider young leaves and remembrance after the tree is cut.
shortened: Although that tree hath outwardly been cut down in the path of the Ancient Beauty, praise be to God that it hath left behind a young tree, green and fresh, as a remembrance.

order.why: Read the branch imagery in a Tablet of Visitation for Haji Siyyid Mihdi Afnan.
shortened: And say: Upon you be glory, upon you be mercy and praise, upon you be grace and bounty, O exalted Branch from the Tree of Eternity and fresh, verdant Twig from the Lote-Tree of the Uttermost Boundary!

order.why: Keep the leaf’s flight in the gravestone text for the Bab’s wife.
shortened: Verily, the exalted leaf hath heard the call of the divine Lote-Tree and hath taken her flight unto it.

order.why: Read the remembrance of a woman who heard and returned to nearness.
Consider the visible dwelling and enduring dwelling associated with relatives.
Read grafting as an image of connection.
Consider the reported counsel about roots and nourishment addressed to Sarah Farmer.
Keep the warning against judging a tree by a leaf’s discordant words.
shortened: If you see an unharmonious movement or hear an unreasonable word, you must look to the root of the Blessed Tree, not its leaves, for the Tree is firm and growing and in the utmost freshness and verdancy, and ere long will bear delicious fruit and cast its shadow upon the horizons.

order.why: Ask what qualities befit relationship to the Tree.
Read a family’s relation to firm roots, lofty branches, and continuing fruit.
Consider the fruits of certitude and the growth of good earth.
Hear the hope that a branch will become holy.
Read the prayer for a branch’s freshness through rain.
Keep the blessing and light addressed to a branch.
shortened: O branch sprung from the Blessed Tree! Upon thee be the glory of God, His light and His radiance. May He illumine thy face with the splendor of the All-Merciful in the heart of contingent being. Verily, He is powerful over all things.

order.why: Read the dove’s melodies and gratitude in a personal address.
Consider the leaf’s thanks for belonging to the Tree.
Read the leaf’s gratitude for its origin.
Hear the invitation to fly to the holy meads and sing among branches.
shortened: Fly rather, in holy meads and chant thy melodies upon the branches of the Lote Tree beyond which there is no passing.

order.why: Read the nameless lover finding a nest.
shortened: Rather, become nameless and traceless in the sea of being content with God, and in the desert of divine love hasten forth lost and bewildered, so that you may find your head and refuge in the divine Kingdom, and make your nest and dwelling in the highest branches of the Lote-Tree of the utmost boundary, and attain the desire of your heart and the comfort of your soul.

order.why: Keep the metaphors of hearing, speech, and the nightingale attributed to the letter.
shortened: I swear by the Most Great Name that if a deaf and mute person rises to praise the Truth, he will speak with an eloquent and articulate tongue and, like the nightingale of the garden of divine knowledge, will warble melodies in diverse modes upon the branches and twigs of the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing.

order.why: Read the prayer for refuge as a bird finding its nest.
Hear the prayer to dispel grief and bring joy to stirring leaves.
Consider the prayer of love for a branch of the Tree of unity.
shortened: O my God and my Hope! Thou knowest my secret and my public self, my hidden and manifest being, and art aware of the extent of my love and the intensity of my devotion to the branch of Thy divine Lote-Tree, the twigs of Thy Tree of Oneness, and the offshoot of Thy Tree of mercifulness.

order.why: Extend the prayer’s care to roots, branches, and leaves.
Read meek servitude beside the fire and firmly rooted Tree.
shortened: This is Your meek servant whose neck is bound by the chain of servitude to Your exalted threshold and bondage to Your lofty presence, and who has come to You in humility and submissiveness, with a broken heart, turning toward Your merciful Kingdom, deriving the fire of guidance from Your unique Tree whose root is firm and whose branch extends into heaven.

order.why: Hear the prayer for separation’s fire to become reunion’s light.
Consider the fire in hearts and the light upon the Mount.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy light which hath shone forth upon the world, and by the fire of Thy Lote-Tree whereby the hearts of the nations have been set ablaze, and by the lights of Thy Manifestation and the Call raised upon Thy Mount, to aid Thy servants to turn toward the lights of Thy countenance.

order.why: Read the prayer to turn toward the horizon and hear the rustling.
shortened: O Lord! Thou beholdest me turning away from all else save Thee and advancing toward Thy most exalted horizon, the Station wherein was raised the rustling of the Sadratu'l-Muntaha.

order.why: Keep the hope of circling the Tree as a devotional aspiration.
shortened: We beseech God, blessed and exalted be He, to ordain for thee that which will exalt thee through His Name amongst His servants, and to write down for thee the reward of him who circumambulated the Sadratu'l-Muntaha in the Most Exalted Paradise.

order.why: Hear sacrifice and the Tree’s rustling in prayer.
Consider the Tree receiving sun and rain through bounty.
Read the prayer that a branch may bear fruit.
Bring the imagery into counsel for oneself before others and perseverance amid hatred.
Close the linked readings with the insistence that the Tree’s fire have visible effects in the world.
shortened: You must be so enkindled by the fire of the Sacred Tree that its effects become manifest and evident in the world.

order.why: End with the supplied Aqdas note explaining the Islamic and Bahai uses of Sadratu’l-Muntaha.

questions: What different kinds of shelter and nourishment does the tree image offer in these readings?
How does a tree that speaks, burns, or carries birdsong change the way we imagine revelation?
What do the Qur’anic verses about the Lote Tree and Revelation’s healing leaves add to your reading of this subject?
How do the relationships of roots, branches, leaves, and fruit illuminate responsibility within a community?
What might it mean to receive nourishment from a spiritual source while making its effects visible to others?
Where do the neighboring images of physician, gardener, educator, pen, and sun deepen or challenge what a tree can express?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 53:14–16 · The Lote Tree and refuge
references.note: Read verses 14–16, using the next-verse links: the Lote Tree at the furthest boundary, the nearby Garden of Refuge, and the covering of the Tree. Compare the passage’s setting of nearness and limit with the compilation’s uses of Sadratu’l-Muntaha. Keep the Qur’anic scene and the Bahai interpretations distinguishable while considering their shared imagery.

references.label: 2 · Revelation 22:1–2 · Leaves for the healing of nations
references.note: Read the river of life, the Tree bearing fruit through the year, and its leaves serving the healing of nations. Compare this picture with the compilation’s fruitful branches and its shelter for peoples of East and West. What makes the image both sustaining for individuals and expansive in its concern for humanity?
